This information report summarizes a continuous improvement investigation to mitigate the concern from nearby residents about noise that originates from the city's snow management sites, which is primarily due to tailgate salami from snow hauling trucks.
The city currently operates three snow management sites. The sites are located at the Civic Operations Center or COC on Wana Skayland Road and the North End of Central Avenue.
The report provides information on noise complaints received from nearby residents over the last two winter seasons.
The current approach to mitigate noise and tailgate salami in at the snow management facilities.

Past public engagement process regarding general noise at the COC previously gathered by the planning and development department as part of the Montgomery Place local area plan approaches and other jurisdictions and noise by law implications as part of an industrial residential interface study that will begin in 2022.

The planning and development department will be completing a noise monitoring within the next six to 12 months that will include measurements of circle drive as part of the implementation work from the Montgomery LAP.

The roadways fleet and support department plans to partner on this noise study project to collect noise data from the COC's no management site to better understand the potential noise propagation to the nearby neighborhood.
The administration will further evaluate noise mitigation options if the study confirms that snow management operations cause sound levels to exceed the nuisance threshold.

Unless otherwise directed the following improvement options will also be implemented prior to the next winter additional large no tailgate salami signs will be installed at the entrances to the three snow management sites and a noise reduction awareness campaign with a goal of providing no tailgate salami and educational and awareness materials to site users.
Deliverables may include a video and targeted advertising leading into next winter.
